title: 2006 AMC 10A Problem 20
statement: Six distinct positive integers are randomly chosen between \(1\) and \(2006,\) inclusive. What is the probability that some pair of these integers has a difference that is a multiple of \(5?\)

solutions.text:
Group the integers by their remainder modulo \(5.\) There are only \(5\) possible remainders but \(6\) integers, so by the Pigeonhole Principle two share a remainder.

Their difference is then a multiple of \(5.\) This always happens, so the probability is \(1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
